newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- The office of Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa may introduce the United Nations definition of "national security" into the proposed Public Order Ordinance and Societies Ordinance in order to dispel fears.
-- The Legislative Council passed the 1997/98 budget with 23 votes against, the largest number of "no" votes ever.
-- APPLE DAILY -- There are a thousand dangerous canopies in Hong Kong like the one whose collapse killed a street sleeper on Wednesday, and there is no deadline when they will be torn down.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- China received international support to once again defeat an anti-China motion at the U.N. Human Rights Commission.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - The row over right of abode seems certain to run until the last hours of British rule after Governor Chris Patten vowed to publish rival legislation if China tables a bill in the provisional legislature.
-- Hong Kong and mainland regulators reached a consensus on rules governing the listing of red chips, but much uncertainty remains over the exact role Chinese regulators will play.

-- HONG KONG STANDARD - Municipal councillors and district board members from the Democratic Party will stage a walk-out at a briefing by the Chief Executive's office on the "Civil Liberties and Social Order" consultation document.
